reviews.text: This app is showing me sites on forest road 153 but says they’re on forest road 132. 132 is drivable in a car 153 is not. What the heck? So I don’t think I’ll be trusting this app at all.

reviews.title: They charge yearly subscription upfront
reviews.text:
I was charged upfront for a full year subscription. I asked for a refund right away. I requested it on Apple's website several times, called Apple Support, and emailed the developer. The developer never helped me, and I still have not gotten my money back.

Be careful before you subscribe. The whole year is charged at once, and getting help afterward is almost impossible. If you want to try this app, choose monthly or cancel any trial early so you don't get stuck like I did.

Developer: please contact me and fix this.

reviews.title: Good app, ridiculous price
reviews.text: Useful info for campers but got tricked into paying $59.99 for an annual subscription I never wanted (I used this app once). Beware of another app trying to trick you into an overpriced subscription you’ll forget about.

reviews.title: Misleading Cancelation and Trial Process
reviews.text:
I cancelled my PRO subscription before the trial ended and received a confirmation saying I would "no longer be charged." Yet I was still charged. I had to cancel it a second time before the cancellation actually took effect. This is not transparent and feels very misleading.
Be careful with the free trial and cancellation process.

reviews.title: Inaccurate Campsite details
reviews.text: Got the 7 day free trial from an ad and it had completely inaccurate campsite pricing details for every park in my region. It listed ALL the Suffolk County, NY parks as being free tent camping but when I called the county parks to double check this I was told that EVERY county park with overnight campgrounds costs around $40 per night if you don’t have a resident permit which in fairness only costs $30 and is good for 3 nights.

reviews.title: Poor Scanner

I have a few other options to switch over to. And oddly enough my free apps have given me way better availability alerts than Dyrt. If these alerts actually worked I’d never let go of this app since I’ve used it so heavily the past year.

Now I can’t get anyone to respond to me regarding the auto billing. I have to go through the process of disputing the charge with my credit card. I really wanted this app to work, but it’s just a hub for information.

reviews.title: Sneaky trial billing. Use ioverlander instead.
reviews.text: I downloaded this app in March for trial, never even used it once. Three months later, they silently hit my card with a $60 annual charge. Technically legal, it’s predatory to bury a 90 day conversion in the fine print without giving email about subscription or before billing. If you want to find great campsites without worrying about accidental pay walls or hidden subscriptions, ioverlander offers same services for free & its community driven!

reviews.title: Added campgrounds that are not campgrounds
reviews.text: Recently I noticed that many “first come first serve campgrounds” have been added to the map in Colorado.  In attempting to visit these spots I’ve found nothing that resembles a campground.  Most of the time they’re trailheads or near dispersed camping areas, but rarely have they been legal places to sleep.  Reviews at these newly added campgrounds can typically confirm this with several users stating they wasted their time attempting to camp there, but the effort I must go through to verify a campground’s status by recent reviews is annoying.  Not to mention wasting hundreds of dollars in fuel driving to campgrounds that don’t exist.  At the very least these “sites” that your algorithm has identified should have a unique label so I can filter them out.  I’ve appreciated your interface as a Pro member for years, but don’t plan on renewing as there are now better alternatives.

Might ask my bank to dispute it honestly.

reviews.title: Did I miss something?
reviews.text: I was looking for a routing app that could ensure I don’t get trapped on roads or bridges that I can’t fit through. It’s exactly what this app advertised however, once I subscribed, I tried to research how to put in my RV height, and it said these features are not yet available. Simple. Don’t advertise what you don’t do.

reviews.title: I’m confused over what this app is supposed to do
reviews.text: I mean I get it’s supposed to find campgrounds but it’s hardly quicker than Google.  And arguably less informative from a review respective.  It’s hard to navigate.  Still struggling to find out how I can search by amenities.  Or campgrounds that will accommodate larger trailers.  We signed up because it was a year free going to the RV show.  I can’t imagine paying $60 a year for this.  No way.  Maybe a one time couple bucks.   All these companies are so eager to drive their customers towards poverty.  Holding their hands out for recurring bills.
